title: QUIC RFC 9000 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED Frame Focused Proof Work Item
summary: Prove the RFC 9000 Section 19.13 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame type, Stream ID field, and Maximum Stream Data field trace tail.
planned_changes:
- Add a focused STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED requirement-home helper for exact field encodings, trailing-frame consumption, parser assertions, and formatter assertions.
- Add focused positive, edge, negative, and fuzz-linked proof for the STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED type and both variable-length integer fields.
- Add direct focused proof that Stream ID preserves the blocked stream and Maximum Stream Data preserves the blocked stream offset, including maximum 62-bit varint values.
- Add STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED parse and format coverage to the existing QuicFrameCodec benchmark suite.
- Link the focused proof to dedicated architecture, work-item, and verification artifacts.
verification_plan: Run the focused S19P13 requirement-home filter, run a Release build, run the QuicFrameCodec benchmark Dry job for STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED parse/format methods, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Closing receiver-side send-only stream termination for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S19P13-0002.
Adding public flow-control tuning or receive-window APIs.
Replacing the span-backed frame-codec hot path.
completion_notes: Completed as focused parser/formatter, field-boundary, and benchmark proof over the existing STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame codec seam.
